messages.subject: RE: SQL schema ignored in ODBC DSN [SEC=UNOFFICIAL]
parts:
Hi Rainer,

 

Try running R studio, and run rattle from within Rstudio. Put the user name and password in the script, load your data in r studio, then you can open it up in Rattle, with the rdataset option

 

Regards

Tony

 

 

From: rattle...@googlegroups.com [mailto:rattle...@googlegroups.com] On Behalf Of Rainer Mokros
Sent: Friday, 6 June 2014 11:03 PM
To: rattle...@googlegroups.com
Subject: Re: SQL schema ignored in ODBC DSN

 

Hello Graham,

I have installaled rattle 3.04 on an ubuntu 14.04 and I have instaled the FREETDS ODBC driver to SQL SERVER y use isql and it worked (only if I especify the user and password at command line the odbc.ini don't work or I don't find the correct parameters)

In RATTLE I can't sepecifiy the user an password so I don't can connect to the database.

Googled the last 2 days with no result can you get me a hint ?


Kind regards
Rainer Mokros


On Saturday, February 16, 2013 11:42:11 PM UTC-5, Graham Williams wrote:

I've probably not got all the possible combinations for all of the types of databases working correctly in Rattle for every case yet.

 

As a work-around, copy the command out of the log and paste it into the console, then add the schema and save the result into "ds" for example (rather than crs$dataset). Then choose to load ds as an R Dataset into Rattle.

 

Hope that helps.


Graham Williams

http://togaware.com

 

On 15 February 2013 23:05, Francois Botha <igi...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi,

 

I'm a new user to rattle. I immediately tried to connect through ODBC DSN to our SQL server. The table of value is e.g. MySchema.MyTable. Rattle populated all the table names, but omitted the schema. I therefore could not successfully continue. In the log, I could see that the schema was omitted and the query that was generated was "SELECT * FROM MyTable" instead of "SELECT * FROM MySchema.MyTable"

 

regards

Francois
